Hi Soojin,

Per our intake call this morning, BrightRetail's security team asked us to collect evidence on all 3rd-party and first-party marketing pixels firing on their storefront (www.brightretail.com) as part of a GDPR DPIA and vendor review. Specifically they need:

- A current inventory of tags/pixels (vendor, purpose, signal type: cookie/localStorage/first-party header)
- The consent gating behavior for EU visitors (screenshots and the JS event that indicates consent)
- Any data retention/subprocessor notes for analytics/ads vendors (e.g., Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, Segment)
- Confirmation of whether any pixel transmits PII or user identifiers that could be tied to a person

Can Redwood provide the inventory and a brief statement on how consent gating is respected at runtime? Also, BrightRetail legal will want to confirm whether a DPA/SCCs are required for any of the vendors and whether Redwood has a documented DPIA template they can use.

If you can send the inventory and screenshots by end-of-week (Fri 2/13) that would keep the review on schedule. We can accept a Drive link or PDFs.

Thanks,
Marta Kline
Lead Privacy Auditor
Privacy Consult LLC

Hi Marta / BrightRetail team,

Thanks — we can do this. Sending an initial inventory and evidence dump below; we'll follow up with a short statement on consent gating and retention. For context: BrightRetail is using our Hosted API for product recommendations and our JS storefront integration (redwood-bridge.js) is optional — in this engagement pixels come from a mix of BrightRetail first-party tags and third-party marketing vendors.

Attached: cookie-scan-report.pdf (automated crawl of www.brightretail.com showing network calls and DOM tag map), privacy-policy-v3.html (site policy snapshot), dpia-template.docx (our DPIA suggested template).

Short answers up front:
- Inventory: see attached report (sheet 1: first-party, sheet 2: third-party). Key vendors observed: Google Analytics (GA4), Meta Pixel, Segment, Hotjar, DoubleClick.
- Consent gating: BrightRetail's CMP triggers a dataLayer event 'consentGranted' for 'marketing' and 'analytics'. Redwood's own hosted API does not inject marketing pixels; we process API calls server-side and only set server-side cookies for session routing (opaque session id).
- PII: We do not detect any pixel sending raw PII (email, name). Some vendor calls include an opaque user_id/session_id which is hashed at BrightRetail's side; that's customer-controlled.

Next steps: Laura (Legal) and Rishi (Security) — can you confirm the DPA/SCC posture and whether our dpia-template is suitable for BrightRetail to adapt? Also note the client asked for screenshots of the EU consent dialog — Marta, we'll upload those by EOD 2/13.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Soojin — quick read: the inventory looks standard. A few notes for the review: 

- DPA/SCCs: Redwood has a standard DPA template and we execute SCCs for EU contracts by default when required. For BrightRetail specifically, they need to confirm flow to third-party ad vendors; if BrightRetail is passing hashed email or any persistent identifiers to Meta/GA, they should have SCCs and a controller-processor mapping. Redwood is a processor for Hosted API usage; vendors called from the client-side (pixels) are the client's responsibility.

- HIPAA: Not applicable here unless BrightRetail is capturing health info on the storefront. If any forms collect sensitive categories, escalate to Security.

- DPIA template: dpia-template.docx is fine as a starting point but suggest adding a section 'client-side tag risk' to capture how third-party pixels can bypass consent. I'll add comments to the Drive copy.

I'll prepare a short sign-off note stating: "Redwood does not deploy marketing pixels from its hosted execution paths; any client-side pixels are configured and controlled by the customer. Redwood's hosted API transmits model outputs and session metadata to downstream subsystems under contracted controls."

Will upload annotated DPIA template and a short sign-off by EOD 2/14.

-Laura

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarification requests after reviewing the scan: 

1) There are repeated calls to a /track endpoint on redwood-hosted subdomain (api.redwood.com/prod/track) that appear to set a first-party cookie _rw_sess for routing. Can you confirm whether that cookie or header includes any persistent user identifier or is it a pure opaque session key? Does Redwood have a retention policy for session cookies?

2) For GA4 calls we see client_id populated. Is that client_id generated on the client or proxied via BrightRetail's backend? If proxied, will BrightRetail have access to raw client identifiers (so they can link web behavior to CRM)?

3) BrightRetail legal asked whether Redwood can provide a short template statement for their privacy policy explaining that third-party marketing tags are controlled by the merchant and that Redwood's server-side processing does not share PII with ad vendors.

If you can answer these three points and upload screenshots of the CMP consent flow (EU path) we'll close the evidence collection and move to DPIA drafting.

Best,
Marta

Hi Marta / BrightRetail,

Answers below:

1) _rw_sess cookie: opaque session identifier only. The cookie value is a cryptographically-random UUID (v4) tied to a short-lived session record. We do not persist email or name in that cookie. Retention: session records are retained for 30 days by default and are purged by rolling retention; longer retention can be contracted. See: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Csoojin-pixel-evidence (retention_policy.md).

2) GA4 client_id: by default GA4 client_id is client-generated in the browser. In BrightRetail's current implementation some analytics calls are proxied via their backend to unify sampling; in those cases the client_id is forwarded unchanged — BrightRetail controls whether they persist or link client_id to CRM. Redwood does not automatically link GA client_id to PII.

3) Privacy policy template statement (short):
"Redwood Inference does not deploy or control third-party marketing tags on merchant storefronts. Any third-party tracking scripts (e.g., analytics, advertising, heatmaps) are implemented and managed by the merchant and their tag manager. Redwood's hosted inference runtime processes API requests server-side and does not forward personal data to advertising vendors. Merchants must ensure appropriate consent mechanisms are in place for EU visitors and maintain their own data processing agreements with third-party tag providers."

Attached: screenshots of the EU consent dialog (screenshots.zip referenced in Drive). Laura has uploaded the annotated DPIA template.

If BrightRetail legal needs a one-page statement for their privacy policy with legalese, Laura can produce that and we can share a DocuSign-ready DPA addendum if needed.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
